per_question.question: Per NPR 7123.1, what is the difference between applying an SE process 'iteratively' versus 'recursively'?
per_question.generated_answer:
Per NPR 7123.1, the difference between the two terms is as follows:

- **Iterative**: This is "the application of a process to the same product or set of products to correct a discovered discrepancy or other variation from requirements" [1].

- **Recursive**: This means adding value to the system "by the repeated application of processes to design next lower layer system products or to realize next upper layer end products within the system structure. This also applies to repeating application of the same processes to the system structure in the next life cycle phase to mature the system definition and satisfy phase success criteria" [1].

In essence, "iterative" refers to reapplying a process to the *same* product to fix errors or deviations, while "recursive" refers to applying the *same* processes across *different layers* of the system structure (moving between lower and upper levels of the system) or across different life cycle phases in order to progressively mature the system design [1].
